Certified reuse of LLM-computed table cells

An AI table column is a materialized view whose definition changes far more often than its data. When the prompt is edited, deployed systems either recompute every cell or reuse all of them blind. sIVM certifies a middle: a set of cached cells whose expected false-reuse rate is bounded by a budget you choose, with probability at least 1 − δ.

The five findings

  1. The decode-noise floor governs everything. At default sampling temperature the model disagrees with itself on 9.5% of rows, exceeding a typical error budget before any edit is made. Pinned to temperature 0 the floor is 5.0%.
  2. Edit intuition misleads. A meaning-preserving synonym paraphrase flipped 8.90% of cells, as much as a genuinely semantic scope change. A formatting-only edit certified 82.6% call savings at α=0.2.
  3. Certified savings are floored by model stability. The certifiable budget cannot beat a stratum's intrinsic flip rate: 3.1% for cached-FALSE cells against 24.1% for cached-TRUE, whose volatility sets the 91.3% savings ceiling.
  4. Stratification is a validity-free lever. Cached-value strata are load-bearing: aggregate-only certification conceals up to 45.2% error in the reused cached-TRUE subgroup.
  5. Column-type stability governs, not edit class. On a 4-way select over long CV text a formatting edit and a real criteria change flip cells at 12.30% and 12.45%, indistinguishable, so the certifier correctly reuses less there regardless of intent.

The α-savings frontier

Mean certified savings over 1,000 sampling replications, per edit pair, as the error budget tightens from 0.2 to 0.02. Savings collapse as α approaches each column's own flip rate, then the certifier refuses outright.

Across 32,000+ labelled cells, 1,000 sampling replications of every configuration, and 396,000 known-rate calibration trials spanning 54 nulls planted just above the budget, no certified stratum's true flip rate exceeded it.

Deployment scale

The boolean column was materialized across the entire 89,184-row corpus: 78,956 billed cells costing $9.31 at $0.00012 per cell, 7.4 hours of model time. The formatting edit was then certified against it. At α=0.2 the procedure spent 225 oracle calls to certify reuse of 81,289 cells, refusing the 7,715-row cached-TRUE stratum.

Sampling cost did not scale with the table. The same procedure on a 2,000-row benchmark spent 135 calls against 225 here, the minimum and the median of one replication distribution (135–405). The schedule stops on evidence about a stratum's rate, which is size-independent, so sample cost is O(1) in n while the certifiable population is O(n).

The certificate was applied, not merely computed: it stamps its identifier on 79,130 of the 81,289 reused cells. The 2,159 it leaves alone are the audited rows already holding freshly computed values, which the apply step refuses to overwrite. A certificate can add a reused value; it can never revert a recomputation.

What the alternatives actually do

Verified-cache similarity carries no cross-version signal. The per-row similarity a semantic cache thresholds predicts flips at chance (AUC 0.468 on formatting, 0.499 on widening). Adding "a version key" to such a cache cannot produce a sound cross-version policy.

Aggregate-only certification silently corrupts subgroups. Run with the same schedule and budget, it certifies 91.0% of cells at 5.99% aggregate error while the reused cached-TRUE subgroup carries 36.1%.

A matched SUPG-style competitor wins on volume and loses on where its errors land. At the same 135-label budget it reused 1,865 cells to sIVM's 1,724, at 6.54% error against 3.36%. The extra volume is 180 cached-TRUE cells, where the per-stratum floor is 24.1%. It also selects 100.0% of the rows it is allowed to, so matched this way it is the guarantee-free baseline wearing a certificate.

The bound we chose is the binding constraint

Every result above spends its error budget through a Maurer–Pontil bound split across six looks by Bonferroni. That choice, not the stratification and not the schedule, is what sets the frontier. Swapping in a Waudby-Smith–Ramdas betting confidence sequence, which is anytime-valid and so needs no split across looks, inside the same procedure over the same labels:

Empirical-Bernstein–Serfling (without replacement)8 / 20––0.166

More certificates, more savings, and a third fewer oracle calls, simultaneously. The widest single gap is the scope-widening edit at α=0.1: 18.1% savings for 1,485 calls becomes 72.0% for 405.

Validity first. A tighter bound only counts if it is still a bound. Over 72,000 planted-rate trials, no null configuration's certification rate is demonstrably above δ: the worst is 2.5% against a per-stratum δ of 0.05, and 0 of 18 nulls have a 95% CI entirely above it. Maurer–Pontil scores zero on that test, and the distance between zero and 2.5% is exactly the point: the conservative bound leaves nearly all its budget unspent, and a clean stratum costs it 360 draws where the sequence needs 180.

The paper reports this as an ablation rather than repinning on it, because the headline results and the deployment run were certified under Maurer–Pontil. An earlier draft asserted the opposite of all of this without measuring it.

A negative result we are keeping

Refining strata by embedding interaction does not pay. Across all 40 shared configurations the finer value×embedding-tertile stratifier is better in 1 and worse in 16; on the headline pair it certifies 61.4% against 82.6%. Its validity is unconditional, since any stratifier frozen before sampling preserves the guarantee. Its power is not: the δ/K split is never repaid on these columns. We report the direction rather than tuning until it inverts.

Honest limitations

A second, weaker model family has a 36.6% self-flip floor, 5.0% for our primary model, and is refused at every budget. That is the theory's own prediction, not a counterexample: a model that cannot reproduce its own answers cannot support certified reuse, and the procedure detects it cheaply instead of certifying something unsafe. The quantitative frontier is therefore model-specific even though the structure held on both.

Bonferroni across strata and looks is sound but conservative. Equivalence is exact-match, so free-text columns need a calibrated judge. Certificates are scoped to a pinned model snapshot and say nothing about provider drift. And the empirical-Bernstein bound is stated for i.i.d. draws while sampling is uniform without replacement; we carry that gap as a stated assumption rather than claiming it closed.
